Particle Distance

Adjust Particle Distance

- Using the  Transform pattern tool, select the Pattern to be edited.

- The quality of the 3D Garment increases as the size of the Particle Distance decreases.

results.name: Particle Distance Setting
results.title: Particle Distance Setting
results.body:
Objective

Particle Distance refers to the average distance between the points that make up a Garment Pattern, in other words, size of the mesh. The Garment quality and Simulation speed depend on the Particle Distance. Therefore set the value at 20mm when making a Garment and dressing it on an Avatar for faster working process, and set it under 5mm to enhance the Garment quality once it is completed. 


Location

Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Particle Distance


Operation

  1. Select Pattern(s).

  2. Follow the indicated guideline below:

    Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Particle Distance

  3. Input desired value for the Particle Distance. (Minimum '0.8' to maximum '700.0')

  4. Press Enter on keyboard to apply.

results.name: CLO runs very slowly when I edit 3D Garment with Particle Distance 5. What should I do?
results.title: CLO runs very slowly when I edit 3D Garment with Particle Distance 5. What should I do?
results.body:
Question

CLO runs very slowly when I edit 3D Garment with Particle Distance 5. What should I do?

 

Answer

For all 3D garment simulation programs, its simulation speed varies depending on the number of meshes in a single file. More meshes there are, slower the speed is. On the other hand, less meshes there are, faster the speed is.

When Patterns' Particle Distance is set to 5, the program naturally slows down due to increase of the number of meshes in a single file. Therefore, we STRONGLY insist you to increase the Particle Distance to 20 when editing 3D Garments and decrease it to 5 when the 3D Garment is fully completed. Then, simulate for about 1~2 minutes.

 

Does CLO still run slowly though Patterns' Particle Distance is set to 20?

  • This may happen when a Pattern is huge (e.g. flare skirt patterns,) because regardless of the Particle Distance value, bigger Patterns contain more meshes.

  • Also, due to difference in their intrinsic character, the program speed may reduce when Patterns' mesh structure is set to Quadrangular. Please refer to Quadrangular/Triangular Mesh manual and configure mesh type as Quadrangular ONLY when needed.


  • Moreover, program speed is also influenced by hardware specification. Please check out suggested specification here.

results.name: Displacement Map (ver5.1.0)
results.title: Displacement Map (ver5.1.0)
results.body:
Objective

Express thickness or bumpiness of fabrics or textures. Applied result can be only checked in the Render window.


Location

Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select from the Fabric List) ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Displacement Map

 

Operation

  1. Follow the indicated path below:
  2. Click the  Browse button to add a displacement map and modify below settings as needed. 

    Displacement Map

    As displacement maps are grey-scaled, their height is determined by the level of darkness of the grey color.

    📝 Note: Increase the image resolution and apply the Gaussian Blur effect to express the texture smoothly.  

    Amount

    Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. The white area of the displacement map shows the maximum height.

    e.g.) When the Amount is set to 10mm, the height for each color differs as below:
     White 10mm, Grey 5mm, Black 0mm
    Clipping

    Adjust to delete all geometries below the Clipping value.

    e.g.) When you want to delete geometries of the certain area:
    Particle Distance

    Adjust the Particle Distance of newly created meshes.

    📝 Note  As more memory is used for lower Particle Distance, it is recommended not to set the Particle Distance below 1 for a wide area.

    Keep Continuity

    Extend the adjacent face to eliminate the boundary line.

    📝 Note: Only applicable to Welded OBJs.

results.name: Hi/Low-Resolution Garment
results.title: Hi/Low-Resolution Garment
results.body:
Objective

Enhance or lower the resolution of Garments. Use this function to enhance the Garment completion in order to emphasize reality and higher quality of a Garment and on the other hand, reduce it for faster adjustments.

 

Location   

Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶Hi-Res Garment / Low-Res Garment 

3D Toolbar ▶ Hi-Res Garment / Low-Res Garment


Operation

  1. Follow the indicated guideline below:

    Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶Hi-Res Garment / Low-Res Garment 

    3D Toolbar ▶ Hi-Res Garment / Low-Res Garment

    → Hi/Low-Res Properties window appears. 

     

  2. Adjust the value for each item.

     


     

  3. Click OK button.
    → The adjustments are now being applied.
     
  4. Activate the Simulation.
    → The adjustments are now being applied to Garment Simulation.

List of Contents

Hi-Res Garment

Hi-Res Garment Settings

 

Hi-Res Garment



- Improve general quality of the 3D Garment after completion.

- Select the  Hi-Res Garment tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Hi-Res Garment.


Hi-Res Garment Settings



- Select the  Hi-Res Garment tool from the 3D Toolbar and the Hi-Res Properties window will appear.

  • Garment
    • Particle Distance
      - Change all Patterns’ Particle Distance to 5mm.

      - Modify Tolerance to decide the range of Particle Distance so that only Patterns with corresponding Particle Distance value will be affected. Patterns with Particle Distance value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected.

    • Add’l Thickness - Collision 
      - Change all Patterns’ Add’l Thickness – Collision to the default value, 1mm.

      - Modify Tollerance to decide the range of Add’l Thickness - Collision so that only Patterns with corresponding Add’l Thickness - Collision value will be affected. Patterns with Add’l Thickness - Collision value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected.

  • Avatar
    • Skin Offset
      - Change all Avatar’s Skin Offset to the default value, 0mm.

      - Modify Tolerance to decide the range of Skin Offset so that only Patterns with corresponding Skin Offset value will be affected. Patterns with Skin Offset value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected.

  • Simulation
    • Simulation Quality
      - Change the Simulation preset to the default setting, Complete (Nonlinear).

      - When fabric items other than the Default Fabric is used to the Patterns, the Complete (Nonlinear) Simulation preset shows more realistically accurate length and wrinkles of the 3D Garment. Since the Simulation speed decreases when the Simulation preset is changed to Complete (Nonlinear), it is advised to change to the respective preset only when improving the 3D Garment quality.

results.title: Low-Res Garment
results.body:
List of Conetents

Low-Res Garment

Low-Res Garment Settings

 

Low-Res Garment


- Decrease general quality of the 3D Garment.

- Select the  Low-Res Garment tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate and select Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Low-Res Garment.


Low-Res Garment Settings


- Select the  Low-Res Garment tool from the 3D toolbar and the Low-Res Properties window will appear.

  • Particle Distance

    - Change all Patterns’ Particle Distance to 20mm.

    - Modify Tolerance to decide the range of Particle Distance so that only Patterns with corresponding Particle Distance value will be affected. Patterns with Particle Distance value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. The default Tolerance range is 5mm to 20mm.

  • Add’l Thickness - Collision 

    - Change all Patterns’ Add’l Thickness- Collision to the default value, 2.5mm.

    - Modify Tolerance to decide the range of Add’l Thickness- Collision so that only Patterns with corresponding Add’l Thickness - Collision value will be affected. Patterns with Add’l Thickness - Collision value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected.

  • Skin Offset
    - Change all Avatar’s Skin Offset to the default value, 3mm.

    - Modify Tolerance to decide the range of Skin Offset so that only Patterns with corresponding Skin Offset value will be affected. Patterns with Skin Offset value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected.

  • Simulation Quality

    - Change the Simulation preset to the default setting, NORMAL.

- To decrease the general quality of the 3D Garment only with the desired options, toggle off options as needed.

- Select OK. The Simulation icon will change.

- Activate the Simulation to apply the settings.

 

 

Go back to the List of Contents

results.title: Select All With Same Property
results.body:
List of Contents

Select All with Same Property

Select All with Same Property from Pop-Up Menu

Select All with Same Property from Property Editor

 

Select All with Same Property

- Select all Patterns will the same property.

- Right-click on the Pattern and select Select All with Same Property from the pop-up menu, or select the same option in the property editor.

Selected All with Same Property from Pop-Up Menu


  • Particle Distance
    - Select the  Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over Select All with Same Property and select Particle Distance from the pop-up menu.

    - All Patterns with the same particle distance will be selected.

  • Layer
    - Select the  Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over Select All with Same Property and select Layer from the pop-up menu.

    - All Patterns with the same layer will be selected.

  • Fabric
    - Select the  Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over Select All with Same Property and select Fabric from the pop-up menu.

    - All Patterns with the same fabric will be selected.

Select All with Same Property from Property Editor

- Select the Pattern from the 2D window.

- Navigate to the Property Editor and find Simulation Properties. Right-click on the options below the Simulation Properties. Click Select All with Same Property to select all patterns with the same respective setting.

 

Go back to the List of Contents
